Q: Using "%" in ArchiveBox config option A:

This is a known pain point with ArchiveBox's config system — it uses Python's configparser under the hood, which interprets % as interpolation syntax (%(key)s). The %% escape is correct per configparser docs, but as you discovered, ArchiveBox's config-rewrite cycle strips it back to % on startup.

The fix: use an environment variable instead of the config file.

Environment variables bypass configparser entirely, so % is treated as a literal character:

export YTDLP_EXTRA_ARGS="['-o', '%(id)s.%(ext)s']"
archivebox server

For a persistent setup (Docker Compose):

environment:
  - YTDLP_EXTRA_ARGS=['-o', '%(id)s.%(ext)s']

Or in a .env file:

YTDLP_EXTRA_ARGS=['-o', '%(id)s.%(ext)s']

Why the config file approach can't work reliably:

  1. You set %% → configparser reads it correctly as % (escaped) → startup works
  2. ArchiveBox re-serializes the parsed value (now %) back to the config file
  3. Next startup reads the un-escaped % → InterpolationMissingOptionError

This is essentially a bug in ArchiveBox's config serialization — it should re-escape % as %% when writing back to the .conf file. You may want to file an issue for that.

Note: If you're running ArchiveBox via systemd, put the env var in your service file under [Service]:

Environment="YTDLP_EXTRA_ARGS=['-o', '%(id)s.%(ext)s']"

Q: In Perl, how can I generate random strings consisting of eight hex digits? A: 
my $rand_hex = join '', map {[0..9,A..F]->[rand 16]} 1..8;

This will generate a string, not just a sequential print (as the method shown above). I'm not a grand master in Perl but for me this is simple, clear and works just fine. Many ways to do such thing but generally the logic remains the same, just the coding examples are different.

print $rand_hex;
# output example
# 4C286F83

Q: Does ferror() indicator remain on when writing to a file? A:

My question is, does the C standard guarantee that the ferror() indicator remains on unless I explicitly call clearerr()

The error indicator for a FILE stream is only cleared in one of two cases:

  • A call to ferror
  • A call to rewind

So in your case, since you don't call rewind, you can be sure that the error indicator will be set if an error occurred at any time before you call ferror.

Section 7.23 of the C23 draft standard mentions the error indicator in several places, and only mentions that it cleared in these two places. It also mentions the function that may set it, specifically:

  • fflush
  • fgetc
  • fputc
  • getc
  • getchar
  • putc
  • putchar
  • fseek
  • fsetpos

While fprintf is not mentioned explicitly as a function that can set the error indicator, it is generally understood that uses one of the above internally that does.
